reason: The cited lines create a GitPython Repo for a validated local path, run repo.git.status(), and return that status text. This establishes reading and returning local repository state, which can include non-public host/repository metadata such as paths, branch/status information, so SECRET is supported. The returned git status text can also contain repository-controlled data such as filenames or branch names, so UNTRUSTED is supported. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution by agent-supplied code; they show a fixed git status operation, so HOSTEXEC is not supported. They also do not show sending data to an attacker-readable external destination, only returning TextContent, so SINK is not supported.
